description: Golden vectors for MarginFuse gateway adapters. Every SDK, in every language, reads this file and asserts against it. Adapters are pure functions with no I/O, which makes them look like the easiest part of the SDK to port and makes them the easiest part to get silently wrong: both hazards below misstate margin without raising an error. Port against these vectors, never by eye.

conventions.input: The provider's raw usage object, exactly as it arrives on the response. `null` means the adapter is called with an explicit null.
conventions.omitInput: When true, call the adapter with no argument at all. Languages with no distinction between absent and null may treat this the same as `input: null`.
conventions.expected.usage: The MarginFuse usage fields. A field absent here must be absent from the adapter's output, not present and zero: a zero token count is a claim that the call used none, which is a different statement from not knowing.
conventions.expected.costUsd: Absent means the adapter must not emit a cost at all, so the event falls through to MarginFuse's own pricing instead of claiming a $0 charge. Present means an exact decimal string, never exponent notation.

hazards: `prompt_tokens` is the TOTAL input count: cached reads and cache writes are already inside it. MarginFuse prices inputTokens, cachedInputTokens and cacheCreationTokens as three separate charges and sums them, so passing `prompt_tokens` straight through charges every cached token twice, at the full uncached rate.

`cost` is a floating point number, and the small values cheap models produce stringify to exponent notation (1.2e-7) in most languages. The API rejects that: costUsd must match ^\d+(\.\d+)?$. Format fixed point to 9 decimal places and trim trailing zeros.

cases.name: cached tokens are not double counted inside prompt_tokens
cases.why: The shape from OpenRouter's prompt-caching docs: 10,318 of the 10,339 prompt tokens were cache reads, so only 21 were billed at the full input rate.

cases.name: cache writes are split out of prompt_tokens too
cases.why: Cache creation is priced differently from both fresh input and cache reads, so all three come out of the same total.

cases.name: the gateway's own cost is carried through as a decimal string
cases.why: Forwarding what the gateway actually charged is what makes the figure exact rather than estimated.

cases.name: a small cost does not become exponent notation
cases.why: String() in most languages emits 1.2e-7 here, which the API rejects outright.

cases.name: a cost at one micro-dollar keeps its digits
a cost of exactly one nano-dollar survives
cases.why: Nano precision is the floor the money type represents; anything above it must round-trip.

cases.name: a zero cost is reported as zero, not omitted
cases.why: A gateway that says a call was free is telling us something. That is different from saying nothing.

cases.name: sub-nano cost rounds to zero rather than inventing precision
cases.why: Money below a nano cannot be represented, so it rounds down honestly instead of being padded into a number the ladder would treat as exact.

cases.name: costUsd is omitted when the response carried no cost
cases.why: Emitting 0 here would claim the call was free. Omitting it lets MarginFuse price the call itself and label the result estimated.

cases.name: an explicitly null usage object is tolerated
cases.why: The adapter is on the response path of a call that already succeeded. It must never be the thing that throws.

cases.name: a missing usage object is tolerated
null fields inside the usage object are tolerated
input tokens clamp rather than going negative
cases.why: If a provider ever reports cached tokens exceeding the prompt total, the honest answer is no fresh input, not a negative charge that would credit the customer.
